definitions.name: collagen type X trimer

definition.text: A collagen homotrimer of alpha1(X) chains; type X collagen triple helices form hexagonal networks (sheets).

definitions.comment: Collagen X trimers have been observed to form hexagonal lattices in vitro, but in vivo they have been found in a fibril associated form (PMID:19693541).

definitions.name: extracellular region

definition.text: The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

definitions.comment: Note that this term is intended to annotate gene products that are not attached to the cell surface. For gene products at the cell surface, consider annotating to external side of plasma membrane ; GO:0009897.

definition.text: A protein complex consisting of three collagen chains assembled into a left-handed triple helix. These trimers typically assemble into higher order structures.

definitions.name: extracellular matrix structural constituent

definition.text: The action of a molecule that contributes to the structural integrity of the extracellular matrix.

definitions.comment: Extracellular matrix glycoproteins may be annotated to this term. PMID:24443019

definition.text: Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.
A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an extracellular matrix.
The volume enclosed by the membranes of the endoplasmic reticulum.

Binding to an identical protein to form a homodimer.

Binding to a protein.

definitions.name: extracellular matrix structural constituent conferring tensile strength

definition.text: A constituent of the extracellular matrix that enables the matrix to resist longitudinal stress.

definitions.comment: Extracellular matrix collagen proteins may be annotated to this term. PMID:29632050, PMID:24443019

definition.text: The action of a molecule that contributes to the structural integrity of an epidermal cutaneous structure.
Binding to a chaperone protein, a class of proteins that bind to nascent or unfolded polypeptides and ensure correct folding or transport.

The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skeleton over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The skeleton is the bony framework of the body in vertebrates (endoskeleton) or the hard outer envelope of insects (exoskeleton or dermoskeleton).

Binding to a transcription coactivator, a protein involved in positive regulation of transcription via protein-protein interactions with transcription factors and other proteins that positively regulate transcription. Transcription coactivators do not bind DNA directly, but rather mediate protein-protein interactions between activating transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery.
